The founder's feedback on the polished Pop out v1–v3: "music is not so great. and also something is off. i am not feeling it… not creative enough or eye catchy, no hooks as such. u can use other tools… i can get paid APIs as well… so first of all instead of rendering the whole video, give me some thoughts, like a sample demo dummy video with all the transitions and the story."

Goal: judge the IDEA, the HOOK, the STORY and the TRANSITIONS fast. Not polish. Fast pre-G2 exploration in curate-motion; fake placeholders are fine where a real-world shot would later be AI video (grey boxes labelled "AI video shot later").

Six animatics, each 8–15 s, 9:16, 540×960 / 30 fps, with big beat labels in a corner, temp music, rough motion that shows each transition's idea:
1. "Nothing to wear": hook "200 clothes. Nothing to wear." over an overflowing messy closet; she sighs, opens Curate, her clothes fly OUT of the phone and hang themselves on a rail; end "Curate. Your closet, finally sorted."
2. "Your camera roll is secretly a closet": fast thumb-scroll through her REAL camera-roll photos; hard freeze on the beat; the outfit peels off her into 3D and lands in a closet grid.
3. "Zee the critic": Zee walks in, looks her outfit up and down, unimpressed meme reaction ("girl… no"); swaps the pieces with a paw tap; "slay". Meme format, funny.
4. "Speed run": "0 → 49 pieces in 3 minutes", huge ticking timer and counter; pieces rain into the grid, accelerating; ends on the full closet.
5. "Outfit-change trend": a hand covers the lens on the beat and the outfit changes, 3 times; each look from the app's real looks, with Zee's pick shown.
6. "Satisfying sort": a chaotic pile of her pieces snaps into a perfect colour-sorted closet, ASMR snaps on each beat.

For each: the hook (first 1 s), beat-by-beat story, transitions list, which shots are AI video later (Veo/Kling/Seedance) vs code motion vs real app footage, music direction (tempo, mood, reference style), why it would stop the scroll.

Music: the Mixkit tracks feel generic to the founder. Pick the best temp track per concept, or find better FREE commercially licensed tracks (check each licence exactly) and record licences. Prepare (do NOT run) paid options with costs: ElevenLabs Music API (Starter), and a licensed library (Artlist / Epidemic Sound). No paid generation without the founder's OK.

prompts.title: Motion studio skill + Pop out v3 to G2
prompts.author: agent:main-session
prompts.body:
Build Curate's MOTION STUDIO SKILL in the curate-motion repo, then take Pop out v3 through its first gates (G1–G2), then STOP for the founder.

Why v2 isn't smooth enough: 30 fps; too few motion-blur samples (fast moves echo); ALL overshoot banned (stiff); some bars too busy; end title ~1 s; the real app on screen too briefly; no scored critic loop.

Implement the article's method as reusable tooling, not one-off scripts:
1. Render contract: frames from time alone, no timers / Math.random (seeded noise only), DEFAULT 60 fps for new ads, a determinism check (render frame N twice, hashes match). Keep Remotion at 60 fps; if too slow or flaky, say so and benchmark.
2. Motion with mass: motion/springs.ts, closed-form springs (pure functions of t), stacking track(t) = v0 + Σ (v_i − v_{i−1}) × spring(t − t_i), presets per object class (ui ~2–4% overshoot, panel ~0%, camera long critically damped, headline lands hard and holds to read, mascot (Zee) bounces on purpose, piece has mass and a slight settle). Bouncy easing banned except mascot. Exponential easing helpers.
3. Motion blur that doesn't echo: 8+ sub-frame samples on fast moves, directional blur from the analytic velocity, a STRIP test (12 frames around the fastest move, checked for echo/ghosting).
4. Measure the music: tools/beats (Python, librosa) → beats.json (bpm, beats, downbeats, hits) stored as each track's beat map in its manifest. - Build it as a NEW ad, ads/pop-out-v2/. Don't change v1.

The philosophy (from a founder-shared brief; follow all of it)
1. Never cut, never fade. Everything transforms. Every shot is made out of the previous one: shapes, type, colour, and the real app UI's own elements morph into the next scene. One continuous line of thought:
   - the outline of a piece popping out of her photo becomes the scan's photo grid;
   - the grid's tiles fold into the Wardrobe's tiles;
   - the last piece collapses into Curate's 4-point star (redraw the mark as a vector so it can morph);
   - the star becomes the end card.
   - Real app footage still appears, but it enters and leaves THROUGH transformations: masks shaped by the previous element, matched geometry, the phone frame forming from a line.

ONE camera language: a locked, straight-on camera that only ever dollies or orbits forward.
3. Rhythm: 120 BPM (or the track's real tempo, beat-mapped), and something changes on EVERY beat. 6. Sound design is half the motion. Keep a music bed from the library, beat-matched (Cat Walk is about 130 BPM; set the BPM from its beat map). Studio product photograph for an online clothing catalog: {desc}. {pres} The item is centered and the entire item is fully visible with a generous empty margin on all four sides; nothing is cropped or cut off at the edges. Clean, light warm-grey seamless paper background, soft even diffused studio lighting, a gentle natural soft shadow. Realistic fabric texture, seams and stitching, true-to-life colour. Exactly one item in the frame: no person, no visible mannequin, no hanger, no props, no price tags, no labels, no brand logos, no text, no letters, no numbers, no graphics, no watermark.

## Placeholders
- {desc}: the piece in plain words, colour first, no brand (e.g. "a plain white cotton crew-neck t-shirt, women's relaxed fit, short sleeves").
- {pres}: how it's shown, one of:
  - ghost mannequin: "Shown as an invisible ghost-mannequin front view, as if worn by an invisible body, with a natural drape and realistic shape; the inside back of the neckline may be visible."
  - ghost mannequin, full length: "Shown as an invisible ghost-mannequin front view of the full length, from waistband to hem, natural shape."
  - flat lay from above: "Laid neatly flat and photographed straight from above."
  - pair at three-quarter angle: "A pair of shoes side by side, photographed at a gentle three-quarter front angle, both shoes fully visible."
  - standing at three-quarter angle: "Standing upright on its base, photographed at a slight three-quarter front angle, strap or handles visible."
  - small item from slightly above: "Arranged neatly in the center, photographed from slightly above."

prompts.author: founder
prompts.why: Pop out v2 (ads/pop-out-v2) meets every rule it sets: no cuts or fades, Geist only, 3 colours + black/white, forward-only camera, a change on every beat of Cat Walk (130 BPM), no 15-frame window near-static, last frame = first (pixel-identical source), banned list avoided, sub-frame + directional blur, coded kick/riser/hits, -14.0 LUFS / -1.9 dBTP. Costs: the end title gets ~1 s, the app footage is smaller and shorter than in v1. Founder to rate after comparing with v1.
prompts.source: Founder-shared brief, relayed by the main curate-app session (8dfb7189) to the Pop out v2 agent, 2026-10-15. Key text as relayed; the founder's original may be longer.
prompts.body:
Make a motion piece as ONE continuous transformation: never cut, never fade. Every shot is made out of the previous one: shapes, type, colour and the UI's own elements morph into the next scene, one continuous line of thought.

Hard constraints:
- ONE typeface.
- At most THREE colours, plus black and white.
- ONE camera language: a locked, straight-on camera that only ever dollies or orbits forward.

Rhythm: 120 BPM, and something changes on EVERY beat.
- The first bar is the hook; then one technique per bar (kinetic type, shape morph, a 2D→3D moment, a UI moment); the last full bar is the strongest moment; the final half bar is the end title.
- The last frame matches the first, so it loops.
- No hold longer than 0.5 s.

Banned: particle bursts, glows, lens flares, camera shake, RGB split, crossfades, generic gradients, bouncy easing, holds over 0.5 s, white flashes, anything template-looking.

Motion: springs (critically damped or overdamped, never overshooting) and exponential easing only. Motion blur that follows speed on fast moves.

Sound is half the motion: a coded soundtrack (Web Audio, OfflineAudioContext) with a soft kick on every beat, a riser into the last bar, and a hit or whoosh on every transformation.

Build it in Remotion or HTML. Render with Playwright at 60 fps, 3 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix. Before the full render, render one frame per beat and check them first.
